newsitem.title: GERMANY: German chocolate plants buy some cocoa butter.
newsitem.headline: German chocolate plants buy some cocoa butter.

text.p: German cocoa bean processors are buying cocoa butter to replenish empty stocks but volumes are limited, traders said on Wednesday.
"It's seasonal -- plants look to the autumn and find that at this stage in the year their cover is thin and they would like to buy butter," one said.
"This has lifted the cocoa butter ratio somewhat but the high pound against the mark remains a deterrent," he added.
Elsewhere, comfortable crop supply fundamentals discouraged bean purchases and the industry's sentiment suffered under the impression of sluggish retail sales.
Chocolate bar maker KJS earlier today said price rises in this market segment planned for the autumn may be scuppered by fierce competition.
London cocoa futures have been mostly range-bound in July after losing 170 stg/tonne within three days in the first week of the month. Sept was last at 1,048 stg, up three.
Traders said origin selling was capping the market at 1,050 while buying was setting in at 1,030.
Third quarter 1997 beans of good West African quality were 3.07 marks/kg cif and fourth quarter was 3.14 marks, up from 3.05-3.06 marks quoted for the second half of the year a week ago.
The cocoa butter ratio over futures rose to 2.44 for the third quarter, up five points. Butter prices liquid ex-works were 7.70 marks.
Sterling was at 3.0010 marks at the Frankfurt exchange fixing on Wednesday versus 2.9670 last week.
